text.tspan: IAM in one picture: WHO (identities) gets WHAT (policies)
One AWS account · IAM is GLOBAL (no region to pick)
email + password used to create the account
all power, cannot be limited by IAM
MFA on, NO access keys, lock it away
Authentication: who are you? (password + MFA, or access keys)
Authorization: what may you do? (policies; everything is DENIED by default)
Free service · least privilege: give only the permissions a job needs
a user can be in many groups
he gets the union of both
assumed by EC2 / Lambda / another account
you write it, reuse it on many identities
embedded in ONE user/group/role, deleted with it
on the resource: S3 bucket policy, role trust policy
Effective permissions = user's own policies + every group's policies (union).
No policy that allows it = implicit DENY. Any policy that says "Effect": "Deny" = explicit DENY, and it ALWAYS wins.
Best practice: attach policies to GROUPS (not users), give each person their own user, use ROLES for AWS services.
